newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine legislator arraigned on rape charges.
newsitem.headline: Philippine legislator arraigned on rape charges.

text.p: A Philippine court on Wednesday set March 12 for pre-trial proceedings against Congressman Romeo Jalosjos, who has been charged with the statutory rape of an 11-year-old schoolgirl.

Jalosjos, who was arrested on January 17 after being on the run for more than three weeks, did not present a plea before Makati Regional Trial Court Judge Roberto Diokno, who conducted the arraignment proceedings and set the pre-trial date.
Under Philippine law, not entering a plea is tantamount to pleading not guilty.
Jalosjos, a House of Representatives member who belongs to President Fidel Ramos's ruling coalition, was arrested by presidential guards at an island hideout 60 kms (37 miles) west of Manila.
He was brought handcuffed to the court on Wednesday, escorted by five prison guards and more than a dozen armed policemen.

A judge ordered the 56-year-old Jalosjos arrested on December 26 on two counts of statutory rape and 12 counts of acts of lasciviousness after a schoolgirl said she had sex with the congressman several times in his apartment in exchange for money.
She was taken to the congressman by her father, who is facing separate charges of child exploitation.

Jalosjos was not in court when the judge issued the arrest warrant and when police went to his house, he had fled. His escape caused a public uproar with newspapers saying it was yet another example of the rich and powerful being immune from the law.
Jalosjos, who has said he is innocent, has petitioned the Court of Appeals to overturn the charges.
